browserSearchPath: CLMS Bio-geophysical Parameters, Vegetation, Vegetation Properties
collectionDescription: The Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (fAPAR) quantifies the proportion of incoming solar radiation absorbed by living vegetation for photosynthesis. Estimates are generated at 10-day intervals, worldwide and at a spatial resolution of about 300 m, with the time series extending from January 2014 to the present.

layers.shortDescription: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation
layers.longDescription: FAPAR quantifies the fraction of the solar radiation absorbed by live leaves for photosynthesis. Values range from 0 to 0.94.

layers.shortDescription: Root Mean Square Error on FAPAR
layers.longDescription: For each dekad, the RMSE quantifies the agreement between the final composite FAPAR value and the individual instantaneous estimates available within the compositing period: the lower the RMSE, the more consistent the dekadal value is with the underlying observations.

layers.shortDescription: Number of valid instantaneous FAPAR values
layers.longDescription: This quality indicator gives the number of valid FAPAR observations available in the compositing window: the higher the count, the more robust the resulting dekadal estimate generally is.

layers.shortDescription: Length of semi-period before the date
layers.longDescription: Length in days of the semi-period before the dekadal date of the compositing window [days].

layers.shortDescription: Length of semi-period after the date
layers.longDescription: Length in days of the semi-period after the dekadal date of the compositing window [days].

The quality flag (QFLAG) summarises, for each pixel, the status of the FAPAR estimate — for instance whether the value is valid, was derived from a sufficient number of observations, or comes from the backup algorithm — allowing users to filter the dataset according to their quality requirements.
